name: read_file
description: Read file contents by line range (1-indexed) or entire file. LARGE FILE PROTECTION IS ENFORCED: (1) Files > 500MB are refused entirely — use grep first. (2) Files > 10MB cannot use should_read_entire_file=true — use line ranges instead. (3) Entire file reads are capped at 2000 lines / 200KB content — excess is truncated (truncated=true). (4) Files > 2MB trigger a warning. Response includes: content, lines (returned count), file_size_bytes, total_lines (full file), truncated, warning, read_mode. For range reads also: start_line, end_line, lines_before_range, lines_after_range. ALWAYS check file_size_bytes and total_lines in the response to decide if further reads are needed. Max 250 lines per call for range reads. Use should_read_entire_file=true ONLY for small files (< 2MB, < 500 lines). For large files, always use start_line_one_indexed and end_line_one_indexed_inclusive to paginate. If truncated=true, use line ranges to read remaining content.

target_file.description: The path of the file to read. Use either a relative path in the workspace or an absolute path.

start_line_one_indexed.description: The one-indexed line number to start reading from (inclusive). Required when should_read_entire_file=false. Default: 1.

end_line_one_indexed_inclusive.description: The one-indexed line number to end reading at (inclusive). Max 250 lines from start_line. Required when should_read_entire_file=false. Default: start_line + 249.

should_read_entire_file.description: Read entire file. BLOCKED for files > 10MB. Capped at 2000 lines / 200KB content. Use ONLY for small files (< 2MB, < 500 lines). Default: false.

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this tool is being used, and how it contributes to the goal.

name: search_replace_in_file
description:
Replace text in a file. Provide file_path (absolute path), old_string (exact text to replace), and new_string (replacement text). For moves/renames, use run_bash with mv instead.

CRITICAL: old_string must be unique within the file — include 3-5 lines of surrounding context to disambiguate. The tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence per call; make multiple calls for multiple replacements. To create a new file, use an empty old_string with the full content as new_string.

Verify with read_file before editing. Use absolute paths only.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify (must be absolute, not relative)

old_string.description: The text to replace (must be unique within the file, and must match the file contents exactly, including all whitespace and indentation)

new_string.description: The edited text to replace the old_string

description: Create a new file at the specified path with the given content. Fails if the file already exists.
name: create_file

target_file.description: The path of the file to create. You can use either a relative path in the workspace or an absolute path. If an absolute path is provided, it will be preserved as is.

content.description: The content to write to the new file.

name: run_bash
description:
Execute a bash command. Use is_dangerous=true if the command affects anything beyond the project workspace (system packages, services, network, user config, or requires sudo). Use is_dangerous=false only for workspace-scoped operations (build, lint, test, git). Use is_background=true for long-running commands.

Guidelines: use absolute paths, chain with && for sequential execution, avoid newlines in the command, append | cat if output might use a pager. Dangerous commands will require user authorization.

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this command needs to be run and how it contributes to the goal.

is_background.description: Whether the command should be run in the background

is_dangerous.description: Whether this command affects anything beyond the project workspace boundary — including files outside the project, system configuration, running processes, installed packages, network settings, or user-level dotfiles/shell config. When in doubt, set to true.

name: thinking
description: A cognitive tool for self-correction and deep analysis. Use this IMMEDIATELY when an action fails, an error occurs, or you are unsure how to proceed. Do NOT use this tool to execute actions (like writing files or running commands). Instead, use it to generate a 'Chain of Thought' log to: 1. Analyze the root cause of the error or unexpected result. 2. Brainstorm 2-3 potential solutions with their pros and cons. 3. Select the best solution to proceed. This helps avoid blind retries and infinite loops.

problem_description.description: The error message, failure description, or the problem to be solved.

current_action.description: The action that was attempted and failed, or the current context.

observation.description: Additional context, observations, or what happened.

name: micro_agent
description: Make an isolated LLM inference call with a custom system prompt. Use for reasoning, analysis, or generation that benefits from a fresh context separate from the current conversation. Typical uses: deep code/error analysis, structured output generation (JSON, summaries, translations), self-reflection. Returns raw text from the model.

system_prompt.description: The system prompt that defines the role, rules, and output format for this isolated LLM inference.

task.description: The task description, question, or content to process.

name: deepthinking
description: A deep system analysis tool for complex problems. Performs multi-dimensional analysis (root cause, system impact, constraints, solution architecture) via an isolated, expensive LLM call. Use ONLY when: 1) conventional methods (thinking, micro_agent, repo analysis, sub-agent delegation) have failed, 2) the problem is inherently complex and requires systematic design, or 3) multiple failed attempts indicate a fundamental misunderstanding. Skip for simple issues. Input: context (full problem context, errors, constraints, what has been tried) and goal (specific objective).

context.description: The complete problem context including: execution environment feedback, key errors encountered, problem background, constraints, what has been tried and failed, and any other relevant information needed for deep analysis.

goal.description: The specific objective to achieve. What should the deep analysis produce? A solution design, a debugging strategy, an architectural decision, or a comprehensive plan.

name: delete_file
description: You can use this tool to delete files, you can delete multi files in one toolcall, and you MUST make sure the files is exist before deleting.

name: rename_file
description: You can use this tool to move or rename an existing file.

name: list_dir
description: You can use this tool to view files of the specified directory.

name: print_dir_tree
description: Print a directory tree structure. Automatically ignores common build artifacts, cache directories, dependency folders, and compiled files. Use show_files=false for a concise directory-only overview (includes file counts per directory). Output is truncated per-directory when exceeding max_items.

dir_path.description: The directory path to print the tree for

max_depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse (default: 3). Depth 0 shows only the root directory name.

show_files.description: Whether to show individual files (true) or only directories (false). When false, file counts are shown per directory. Default: true

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to display per directory. Additional items are truncated with a count. Default: 50

ignore_extra.description: Additional directory names to ignore (merged with built-in defaults). Useful for project-specific noise directories.

name: search_by_regex
description: A high-performance search tool powered by ripgrep (rg) designed for large codebases. It supports PCRE2 regular expressions and automatically respects .gitignore rules. Use this tool to precisely locate function definitions, variable references, error messages, or complex code patterns across multiple files.

name: semantic_search
description: Perform semantic search on the repository to find relevant code snippets based on natural language query or code snippet. Returns a list of matches including file paths, symbol names, and code blocks. Use this tool when you need to find specific functionality or implementation details but don't know the exact file or function name.

query.description: The natural language query or code snippet to search for.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return. Default is 5.

name: query_code_skeleton
description: Get the skeleton (definitions of functions/classes without implementation) of specific files. Use this when you need to understand the structure of specific files without reading their full content.

filepaths.description: List of absolute file paths to query skeletons for.

name: query_code_snippet
description: Get the code snippet of a specific function in a file. Use this when you need to read the implementation of a specific function.

filepath.description: The absolute path to the file.

function_name.description: The name of the function to retrieve.

name: ask_user_for_help
description: When you encounter an issue that requires user authorization, confirmation, or input, use this tool to ask the user for help. The tool will pause execution and wait for the user's response. Use this when you need: 1) Authorization to proceed with a potentially risky operation, 2) Clarification on ambiguous requirements, 3) Confirmation before making a significant change. The user's response will be returned directly.

reason.description: A clear explanation of why you are stuck and need the user's help or authorization.

specific_question.description: A specific, concise question to ask the user. This will be shown to the user directly.

suggested_options.description: Optional. Suggested answer options for the user, e.g., 'Approve / Reject / More Info'.

name: agent_exit
description: Exit the agent with a reason. Use this when you are done — whether the task completed successfully, failed, needs clarification, or must be terminated. The reason must explain WHY the agent is exiting.

reason.description: The reason the agent is exiting, e.g., task completed, cannot proceed, blocked by missing information, or must terminate.

name: delegate_browser
description: Delegate a web research task to the Browser-Agent. Use this tool ONLY when the required information CANNOT be obtained from local documentation sources (go docs, python docs, help, man pages, --help, etc.). The Browser-Agent will navigate the web and return findings. Provide a clear, self-contained task description.

task.description: A clear, self-contained research task for the browser agent, e.g., 'Search for the latest documentation on Python's asyncio.run function' or 'Find common solutions for Go error: undefined: sql.NullString'.

name: find_function_callee
description: Find all functions that the specified function calls (its callees). Given a function name, returns a list of functions it invokes, including file paths and line numbers. Useful for understanding what a function does internally.

function_name.description: The name of the function to find callees for

filepath.description: Optional: specific file path to narrow the search (e.g., 'src/main.go')

name: find_function_caller
description: Find all functions that call the specified function (its callers). Given a function name, returns a list of functions that invoke it, including file paths and line numbers. Useful for understanding who depends on this function.

function_name.description: The name of the function to find callers for

filepath.description: Optional: specific file path to narrow the search (e.g., 'src/main.go')

name: git_checkpoint_list
description: List all available git checkpoints for the current coding session. Use this to see what rollback points are available. Each checkpoint represents a saved state of the codebase that you can return to if something goes wrong.

name: git_checkpoint_rollback
description: Roll back the working tree to a specific checkpoint. WARNING: This discards all changes made AFTER the checkpoint. Use git_checkpoint_list first to see available checkpoints. The checkpoint_tag parameter should be the full tag name from the list.

checkpoint_tag.description: The tag name of the checkpoint to roll back to (from git_checkpoint_list)

name: git_checkpoint_create
description: Manually create a git checkpoint at the current state. Use this before attempting risky operations like large refactors, complex merges, or experimental changes. A checkpoint allows you to roll back if something goes wrong.

message.description: A brief description of why this checkpoint is being created
